source: Lantmäteriet Markhöjdmodell 1 m, the published l0 tiles of the johannesberg v2 ground, rendered as hillshade (johannesbergbuild/cache/hs-crop.mjs) with a 10 m legacy grid and read by eye at 10 px/m. A built green is a plateau with banks and a bunker is a pit with a rim, and both survive in a laser DTM when a leaf-off image shows nothing. Centres are good to about ±5 m and radii to ±3 m; each ring is an ellipse on the hole's axis, the same shape build-nine synthesises, at the measured place instead of the routed end. The imagery-traced greens (nine-sat-shapes.json) take precedence where accepted; these fill in where the classifier found nothing.

3.notes: a rounded raised area north-east of the routed end, bounded west by the boundary ditch's bank; the least distinct of the four

4.notes: a round plateau with a continuous dark rim, 12 m north-west of the routed end — unmistakable

5.notes: the mound complex 33 m east of the routed end, which is where a 271 m hole from the 5th tee lands; the imagery shows the same pale rounded complex with the 22 m² sand hollow on its west side

6.notes: the flat raised area south-east of the routed end, behind the pit-and-mound bunker at (-568,-676)
a pit with a bright mound on its south side, 25 m short-left of the laser green; invisible in the leaf-off imagery

refused.1: the routed end sits at the foot of the felled knoll's bank; the ground is smooth and un-terraced for 40 m around and no plateau reads
refused.9: two candidates 30 m apart — the mound complex at (-288,-789), which fits the 5th's card length better and is given to the 5th, and a mottled area at the routed end that does not read as a plateau; kept synthesised
